message.content:
The sea’s “color” isn’t fixed—it varies with depth, water composition, lighting, and what you’re looking at:

| Factor | Typical Appearance |
|--------|--------------------|
| **Shallow coastal waters** | Bright turquoise or aqua when sunlight penetrates clear, sandy bottoms. |
| **Open tropical seas** | Deep sky‑blue or teal where there’s little sediment and plenty of phytoplankton. |
| **Deep ocean (>200 m)** | Dark navy or almost black because very few wavelengths reach those depths. |
| **Polluted or muddy areas** | Greenish‑brown due to suspended particles and algae blooms. |

So while many people think of the sea as “blue,” it actually spans blues, greens, turquoises—and even dark shades—depending on conditions.
